selection_criteria: Applications pass a formal evaluation and a substantive (merit-based) evaluation; the panel may invite selected applicants to an interview

A positive substantive evaluation requires at least 60 points in total, including no fewer than 25 points under criterion 1 and no fewer than 25 under criterion 2
An applicant scoring 0 points under criterion 1 receives a total of 0 and is not evaluated under criterion 2
Financial resources are allocated to the applicants with the highest substantive evaluation scores

applicant_utility.summary: This is a small, merit-driven NAWA scholarship for citizens of high-income countries who want a full-time master's in Poland: PLN 2,000 a month, free tuition at public universities, and a travel grant sized by your home country's distance from Warsaw. The structural catch is that the NAWA application and the university admission are two separate races - NAWA will not help you get a study place, only one application per person is accepted per call, and the whole 2026/27 round is already finished with the ranking list published, so the realistic target is the spring 2027 call for 2027/28 entry.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent bachelor's graduates (degree awarded 2024 or later) from the listed countries with strong grades who can secure their own admission to an English-taught master's at a Polish public university holding a NAWA framework agreement.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality is on the call's country list and that your bachelor's was awarded in a Programme country in 2024 or later
Secure a B2 English or Polish certificate that appears on the call's Annex 3/4 recognised lists before applying
Apply to your chosen university's own admissions system first, within its deadlines - NAWA pays only after you are enrolled
Draft a motivation letter that names the exact Master's thesis topic you intend to research and justifies the university choice
Arrange sworn-translator or Polish consular certification for any document not already in Polish or English
Use the call's model certificate template if you are a final-year student, with GPA, course list, seal and signature all present
common_rejection_risks: Bachelor's diploma issued before 2024 - the recency rule is absolute and final-year students must finish by mid-July of the call year
A language certificate that is not on the call's recognised list, or a level below B2
Foreign grading scales: a GPA converting below 3.55 into the Polish system scores zero on criterion 1 and zeroes the entire substantive evaluation
Scoring below 25 on either criterion even when the total exceeds 60 - both minimums must be met
Assuming NAWA intermediates university admission, or submitting more than one application in a call
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond the PLN 2,000 monthly stipend: full tuition at non-public universities, residence permit and insurance costs, and personal expenses; the one-time travel lump sum is fixed by country of origin (PLN 1,000-6,500).
document_audit: The diploma supplement with the full course and grade list is mandatory, not optional
Final-year applicants must use the exact model certificate from the call's attachments - a home-made letter fails
EU citizens may submit an identity card instead of a passport page; non-EU citizens must use the passport data page
Translations must carry a sworn translator's or Polish consular signature and seal
The scholarship agreement must be signed within 30 days of appearing in the NAWA system, and an annual report is due by 31 October each year
alerts: Only one application per person per call - there is no second attempt in the same cycle
The 2026/27 cycle closed on 29 May 2026 and its results are published; the next call is expected around spring 2027
The scholarship is paid through the enrolled university, so enrolment status drives payment
Applicants who previously held a NAWA second-cycle scholarship are excluded outright
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in the NAWA ICT system, upload scanned or QES-signed documents, submit electronically before the call deadline, then enrol at the chosen university - funding follows enrolment.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an intergovernmental fellowship: you cannot apply directly to UNESCO - your National Commission for UNESCO must select and transmit your file, so the operative deadline is your commission's internal one, not the published 26 May date. If endorsed, the package is unusually complete for a six-month research stay: free tuition at AGH Krakow, PLN 1,800-2,200 per month explicitly covering all living costs and accommodation, return airfare, health insurance, an arrival allowance and a US$120 pocket allowance - you only fund your visa and passport. The 2025 edition is closed and no 2026 edition had appeared as of October 2026, so track unesco.org/en/fellowships for the next round.
applicant_utility.best_fit: BSc, MSc and PhD holders from the 57 invited Member States in engineering and related sciences who can get their National Commission to nominate them and can produce apostilled, English-translated degree certificates quickly.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your country appears in the 57-state Annex II list and that your intended project accepts candidates from your nationality/region
Contact your National Commission for UNESCO months ahead - it sets its own earlier cut-off and may limit how many candidates it forwards
Get degree certificates apostilled or legalised and officially translated into English well before the call opens
Line up two recommendation letters dated within the edition year
Prepare the four-page application form typed in block capitals, with a passport copy and identity photo attached
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to UNESCO instead of through the National Commission - such files are discarded
Missing Apostille or consular legalisation on degree certificates, including for countries that do not recognise the Apostille
Illegible or lower-case form entries, which UNESCO explicitly eliminates from evaluation
Late transmission by the National Commission past the midnight Paris deadline, or an incomplete package
Choosing a project whose Annex III/IV entry restricts eligibility to another region
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Passport and visa expenses are explicitly not funded by UNESCO or the Polish authorities; the monthly allowance is intended to cover all living expenses and accommodation, so costs beyond it (personal travel, extras) are the fellow's own.
document_audit: All four pages of the application form must be completed in English capitals - partial or mixed-case forms fail
Recommendation letters must be dated within the edition year (2025 letters for the 2025 edition)
The identity photo copy is a mandatory attachment that applicants often overlook
Non-native English speakers must attach the UNESCO certificate of language knowledge completed by an authority
After endorsement, the online information sheet must be completed by the same 26 May midnight Paris deadline
alerts: The real gatekeeper is your National Commission for UNESCO, not UNESCO Paris - start there
Selection is decided by the Polish authorities and explicitly takes gender equality and diversity into account
Only 28 fellowships are available across all 57 invited states, so national nomination is the competitive bottleneck
The 2025 edition is closed and no successor had been published as of October 2026
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: File with your National Commission for UNESCO; once endorsed, e-mail the complete application to agh.poland@unesco.org with the two listed addresses in copy and finish the online information sheet by the deadline.
